primitives.note: The core of the kit: 5 weapons, 2 equipped at once (main/off-hand), each with its own Moonlight ammo (50/weapon, 1 per attack, 10 per Q cast), auto-swapping on empty; Phase (W) manually swaps, E only displays the queue.
Each weapon is effectively a separate form: a distinct basic-attack effect (P) and a distinct Q active, swapped in and out as main/off-hand change.
Moonshot, Binding Eclipse, Duskwave's initial cone hit and Moonlight Vigil's initial smite all deal damage on a fixed cast time (or short travel delay), on cooldown.
Duskwave (cone, then a 0.25s-delayed off-hand volley) and Moonlight Vigil (smite, then 0.3s-delayed sky-attacks) each resolve as two separately timed damage instances from one cast.
Calibrum's mark arms the next basic attack for bonus damage; Moonlight Vigil's sky-attacks are a similar armed/delayed attack against each locked-on target.
Infernum's total-attack multiplier (110% AD) and Crescendum's per-Chakram bonus both ride on ordinary basic attacks.
Crescendum's own attack timer is reset once the thrown blade is caught (locks out attacking until then).
Crescendum's held Chakrams: cap 20, 5s expiry refreshed by catching/attacking, diminishing bonus AD per stack (15% down to a 5% floor).
Calibrum's mark is a target-side flag (applied by Calibrum abilities/R) later consumed by the empowered snipe.
Moonlight ammo and mana genuinely bound how many attacks/casts happen in a 15s fight.
Infernum's crit sprays 6 missiles instead of 4; Onslaught/Duskwave's volley/Sentry/R's sky-attacks all crit (Sentry at 100% AS/crit-chance effectiveness); R adds its own extra crit-damage modifier.
Onslaught's attack count scales with bonus attack speed; Crescendum's attack windup is reduced (further on crit); Sentry benefits from Aphelios's attack speed.
Sentry deploys a lunar sentry that autonomously attacks with a copy of the off-hand weapon.

Crescendum's throw-and-return travel time depends on distance to the target; Infernum's secondary/cone bolts require other enemies behind the target, which a single dummy fight does not have; Sentry's activation depends on placement.
Weapon Master: Q unlocks at champion level 2, R at 6 and auto-upgrades at 11 and 16.

needsBespoke.why: A generic rank/level-scaled ability model cannot express: (1) the weapon state machine itself -- which of 5 weapons is main vs off-hand vs reserve, gating which P attack-effect and which Q are active, and changing over the fight as ammo depletes or Phase is toggled; (2) several abilities' damage depends on whichever OTHER weapon is currently off-hand/main at the moment they resolve (Calibrum's empowered snipe always fires with the off-hand weapon; Onslaught/Duskwave/Sentry's follow-ups use the off-hand weapon; R's bonus effect depends on the main weapon at cast time), i.e. cross-weapon dependencies, not a single ability's own rank; (3) Crescendum's per-Chakram bonus is a diminishing, capped, expiring stack curve (15% down to a 5% floor per stack, 20-stack cap, 5s refreshed expiry), not a linear coefficient; (4) Crescendum's attack cadence depends on projectile travel time to and from the target (geometry), not a fixed attack windup; (5) Binding Eclipse is only castable once a precondition (a live Gravitum slow or in-flight projectile) is met, not simply off cooldown.

proposal: Start with the fixed initial loadout: Calibrum main / Severum off-hand, Gravitum/Infernum/Crescendum queued in reserve.

Cast Moonshot immediately to mark the target; the very next basic attack (fired with the off-hand weapon) is then automatically empowered for the mark's bonus damage. Recast Moonshot every time it comes off cooldown while Calibrum remains available.

Auto-attack continuously between casts. Infernum's basic attack (flat +10% AD, no cast needed) and Crescendum's basic attack (growing, if diminishing, bonus AD from held Chakrams) are the highest-value auto-attack states, so once ammo depletion or Phase brings either to main, prioritize sustained auto-attacking over holding them off-hand.

As soon as a Gravitum basic attack has landed or a Gravitum bolt is in flight, cast Binding Eclipse for its magic-damage burst -- it cannot be cast at all before that precondition is met, so do not simply wait for it to come off an ordinary cooldown.
Cast Duskwave as soon as Infernum is main and it is off cooldown: it hits the target directly and then guarantees a further 100% AD off-hand attack 0.25s later.

Cast Sentry as soon as Crescendum is main and it is off cooldown, placed so it can reach the target immediately (minimizing its up-to-20s idle window before it activates); let it attack autonomously for its full active window while continuing to manage other weapons.

Cast Onslaught whenever Severum is main and it is off cooldown, for its 6 (+bonus attack speed) guaranteed attacks; because it locks out Phase and Moonlight Vigil for its 1.75s duration and its own cooldown only starts once it ends, avoid opening it immediately before R would otherwise come off cooldown.

Cast Moonlight Vigil as soon as it is off cooldown regardless of which weapon is currently main, since its own smite and sky-attack damage are large flat contributions either way; if timing is flexible, prefer casting it while Calibrum or Infernum is main, since Severum's and Gravitum's R bonuses (heal, slow/root) add no damage in this fight.
Never hold Moonlight ammo or mana in reserve: with no allies, minions, healing, or crowd control to manage, attacking and casting on cooldown throughout the 15s maximizes damage.
questions: Is it worth manually toggling Phase (0.8s cooldown, 0.25s swap) to force a specific weapon order, versus simply letting the 50-ammo natural depletion cycle weapons on its own?

Right before casting Onslaught, Duskwave, Sentry or Moonlight Vigil, is it worth forcing a specific weapon into the off-hand/main slot given how much their guaranteed follow-up attack's value differs by weapon?

Crescendum's Chakram stacks build fastest from other weapons' off-hand attacks during Onslaught/Duskwave; is it worth deliberately delaying Crescendum's own turn as main to bank stacks first, and how many can realistically accumulate in 15s of casting?

How much of the 15s fight does weapon-reassembly downtime (1s reassembly plus up to a 1.5s Q lockout each time a weapon's ammo hits zero) actually cost at realistic attack speeds, and does that change which weapon order is optimal?
At what champion level and item state is this fight assumed to run? Q/R availability, ammo drain rate relative to attack speed, and how many full weapon cycles fit in 15s all depend on it.
